_: GENERATED — what an authoring tool needs to FIND an operation. The calling table is the .lua beside it.

operations.name: Close a card
operations.description: Closes the card for good. A second close answers the card again.

operations.name: Create a card
operations.description: Issues a virtual card to a connected user, with your company credential. Send an `Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key collects the same card and spends once.

Idempotency-Key.description: Your key for this card. Retry with the same one after a timeout or a `202`.

user_id.description: The connected user the card is for.

amount_cents.description: What the card can spend, in cents. At least 100.

type.description: `single_use` closes after its first approved charge.

expires_at.description: Closes a `multi_use` card at this time, at most 365 days out.

scope_preset.description: Locks a `multi_use` card to AI-lab merchants.

operations.name: Read card credentials
operations.description: The number, expiry and CVC to key into a checkout. Read them at the payment form, never store them, and keep them out of your logs. Each read is audited.

operations.name: Get a card
operations.description: One card, with no number or CVC.

operations.name: List cards
operations.description: Your company's cards in this credential's mode, newest first. Never carries a card number.

limit.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

operations.name: Pause a card
operations.description: Blocks new charges on a multi-use card until you resume it.

operations.name: Resume a card
operations.description: Lets a paused card take charges again.

operations.name: Simulate an authorization
operations.description: Sandbox only. Places a hold without clearing it, and sends `transaction.authorized`. With `outcome: declined` it sends `transaction.declined` instead. A hold larger than the balance is declined with `insufficient_funds`.

amount_cents.description: Defaults to $6.75, or the card's balance if that's lower.

merchant.description: The merchant name on the transaction.

mcc.description: The merchant category code. Defaults to `5812`, a restaurant.

decline_reason.description: The reason on a declined transaction. Defaults to `insufficient_funds`.

operations.name: Capture an authorization
operations.description: Sandbox only. Clears an authorized transaction, for all of the hold or less, and sends `transaction.cleared`.

operations.name: Simulate a charge
operations.description: Sandbox only. Authorizes and clears a charge in one call, and sends `transaction.authorized` and `transaction.cleared`.

amount_cents.description: Defaults to $6.75, or the card's balance if that's lower.

merchant.description: The merchant name on the transaction.

mcc.description: The merchant category code. Defaults to `5812`, a restaurant.

operations.name: Refund a charge
operations.description: Sandbox only. Refunds a cleared transaction, for all of it or part. As on a live card, the refund arrives as a new transaction with a negative amount, and sends `transaction.cleared`. The original transaction doesn't change.

operations.name: Reverse an authorization
operations.description: Sandbox only. Releases a hold and sends `transaction.voided`. A single-use card the hold closed stays closed.

operations.name: Top up a card
operations.description: Raises the limit of a company-funded multi-use card from your company balance. `Idempotency-Key` is required, so a retry never tops up twice.

Idempotency-Key.description: Your key for this top-up. Retry with the same one after a timeout or a `202`.

amount_cents.description: What to add to the limit, in cents. At least 100.

operations.name: Change a card's limit
operations.description: Sets a new total limit on a user-funded multi-use card. A company-funded card is refused with `company_flow_card`: raise it with a top-up instead.

spend_limit_cents.description: The new total limit, in cents. At least 100.

operations.name: Get the company wallet
operations.description: What's on your company balance and what's free to spend, in this credential's mode.

operations.name: Add test money
operations.description: Adds mock money to your sandbox company balance. Sandbox credentials only.

amount_cents.description: What to add, in cents. Up to 10000000.

operations.name: Record consent
operations.description: Records that the user authorized your platform to act on their behalf. Safe to retry — it's idempotent per user, so a repeat call updates the same record instead of creating a duplicate.

terms_version.description: Optional. The version of your terms the user accepted, stored for your audit trail.

operations.name: Refresh the connection
operations.description: Connection access tokens expire after one hour. Exchange the refresh token for a new pair before then. Each refresh returns a **new** refresh token and invalidates the old one — replace the stored token every time.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token from the most recent `/connect/verify` or `/connect/refresh`.

operations.name: Send a code
operations.description: Sends a one-time code to the user by email or phone. Provide **exactly one** of `email` or `phone`. Codes are valid for 10 minutes. If you've designed a connect email in your dashboard, we send that branded email; otherwise we send a default one.

email.description: The user's email address. Provide this or `phone`, not both.

phone.description: The user's phone number in E.164 format (e.g. `+15551234567`). Provide this or `email`, not both.

external_user_id.description: Optional. Your own identifier for the user, stored on the attempt for your reference.

operations.name: Verify the code
operations.description: Checks the code the user entered and, on success, connects the user and returns the token pair to store. Completing the code **is** the authorization — there is no separate approval screen. The returned `access_token` is the **user's connection token**: it acts on behalf of this user (send it as the bearer token to the MCP server to create cards, check balances, and shop as them). code.description: The one-time code the user entered. Always `111111` in sandbox.

operations.name: Create an access token
operations.description: Exchanges your `client_id` + `client_secret` for a platform access token (OAuth2 client credentials, RFC 6749 §4.4). The token lives one hour — when it expires, exchange again; there are no refresh tokens on this grant. Get your credentials in the Agentcard dashboard under **Organization → Developer → Credentials**. A sandbox client mints tokens that act in sandbox; a production client acts in pro

client_id.description: Your client id, from the dashboard.

client_secret.description: Your client secret (`acs_…`), shown once when you create the client.

operations.name: Introspect credential
operations.description: Returns the organization and mode your token acts as. Useful as a health check and to confirm you're pointed at the right credential.

operations.name: Get verification status
operations.description: Polls the current verification status — the alternative to the `identity.verification.updated` webhook.

operations.name: Import a verification (sumsub share token)
operations.description: Import a verification you already ran on your **own Sumsub account** (Reusable KYC). Generate a single-use share token for the Agentcard client id, send it here, and the user skips document capture and the face scan. A successful import drops into the exact same status contract as a fresh verification: poll `GET /api/v2/kyc` or listen for `identity.verification.updated`. Requires one-time partner

share_token.description: A Sumsub share token generated by your account for the Agentcard client id (`POST /resources/accessTokens/shareToken` with `forClientId`). Single-use; expires after its `ttlInSecs`.

user_ip.description: The end user's IP address as your frontend saw it (public IPv4 or IPv6; private or reserved addresses are rejected). Strongly recommended: identity screening checks the applicant's IP, and an IP belonging to a datacenter (such as your backend's) can fail an otherwise valid verification. Pass the address your user connected to you from; without it, your server's own address may be recorded as a las

operations.name: Simulate an outcome (test mode)
operations.description: **Test mode only.** Drives a test-mode verification to a chosen terminal outcome instantly — test verifications never complete on their own. The simulated verdict flows through the same status contract and fires the same `identity.verification.updated` webhook a real review produces, so your status handling and webhook consumer are exercised end to end. Requires a test-mode client credential; live

outcome.description: The verdict to apply. `approved` — verification succeeds. `rejected` — terminal rejection. `requires_input` — a retryable bounce asking for new document photos.

reason.description: Optional end-user-safe explanation carried on non-approved outcomes — it appears as `reason` in statuses and webhook events, exactly like a real review's. It must not name internal providers or identifiers (rejected with `400 invalid_reason`), since it is shown to end users verbatim.

operations.name: Submit information
operations.description: Submits the extra fields requested by a `needs_information` response. Send only the fields listed in `required_fields`; values are trimmed, and a blank value counts as not provided. For a fresh verification, the response returns the `iframe_url` for the face scan. national_id_number.description: The user's national ID or tax identification number for the country that issued their document — for US documents this is the SSN; for any other country it is the national ID / tax number printed on (or associated with) the document. Forwarded to the verification provider only; never stored by Agentcard.

user_ip.description: The end user's IP address as your frontend saw it (public IPv4 or IPv6; private or reserved addresses are rejected). Strongly recommended: identity screening checks the applicant's IP, and an IP belonging to a datacenter (such as your backend's) can fail an otherwise valid verification. Pass the address your user connected to you from; without it, your server's own address may be recorded as a las

operations.name: Upload the back of the id
operations.description: Uploads the back of the document. The response tells you what to do next — this is the branch point of the flow: - `needs_information` → collect exactly the `required_fields` and post them to `/kyc/information`. - `requires_verification` → show the user the `iframe_url` for the face scan. - `rejected` → the document couldn't be verified.

operations.name: Upload the front of the id
operations.description: Uploads the front of the user's identity document as a base64-encoded image. This step acknowledges receipt; the next step (`back`) tells you what comes next. Any upload response may include a `warnings` array with actionable feedback (for example, that the other side of the document is still needed). The response's `extracted` object carries what the document reader pulled off the image — use it

operations.name: Get a transaction
operations.description: One transaction, in the same shape the list returns. The id is the `id` from the list, or the `transaction_id` a `transaction.*` webhook event carries.

operations.name: List transactions
operations.description: Every charge on your company's cards and every Vault checkout your agents opened, newest first, in your credential's mode: sandbox credentials read sandbox transactions, production credentials read live ones. A purchase is listed once.

limit.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

cursor.description: The `cursor` from the previous page. Leave it out for the newest rows.

card_id.description: Only charges on this card. Leaves Vault checkouts out, since they aren't on a card of yours.

created_after.description: Only transactions at or after this ISO 8601 time.

created_before.description: Only transactions before this ISO 8601 time.

operations.name: Disconnect a user
operations.description: Ends your app's connection to a user. Every token your app holds for the user stops working, Vault session links they have not opened stop opening, and their cards stay in their Vault. Idempotent: a second call answers `200` with every count at `0`.

user_id.description: The user's id, as your app stored it when they connected.

operations.name: Fund a user's balance
operations.description: Creates a single-use Apple Pay or Google Pay link the user pays in their own browser. It moves no money by itself. In sandbox no one pays: the test money lands right away and `checkout_url` is `null`.

amount_cents.description: What the user should receive, in cents.

operations.name: Get a funding session
operations.description: Where a funding session stands.

operations.name: Get a user's balance
operations.description: What one user can spend from their own balance.

operations.name: Send a phone code
operations.description: Sends the user the one-time code that funding needs. A verification stays fresh for 60 days.

phone_number.description: The user's phone in E.164, when none is on file.

operations.name: Verify a phone code
operations.description: Checks the code the user read back. In sandbox the code is always `111111`.

code.description: The code the user read back.

phone_number.description: The same number you sent the code to.
